properties.description: Workin' Moms (2017) is a Canadian comedy-drama series created by and starring Catherine Reitman. The ensemble cast includes Catherine Reitman (Kate Foster), Dani Kind (Anne Carlson), Juno Rinaldi (Frankie), Jessalyn Wanlim (Jenny) and Philip Sternberg (Nathan), among others. Produced and directed across seasons by a number of Canadian television directors—including episodes overseen by Catherine Reitman herself and frequent collaborators such as Aleysa Young and Jordan Canning—the show is a single-camera dramedy that follows the professional and personal lives of a group of mothers in Toronto. Combining sitcom rhythms with serialized character development, the series foregrounds themes of motherhood, friendship, identity and work–life balance while pairing incisive, often darkly comic situations with candid emotional arcs. Its tone is at once witty and heartfelt, giving viewers both laugh-out-loud moments and sincere examinations of contemporary parenting and ambition.
properties.plot_summary: A tight-knit group of friends in contemporary Toronto negotiates the competing demands of career, romantic relationships and parenting. The central through-line follows Kate Foster, a PR professional trying to re-establish herself after becoming a mother, while her friends confront fertility struggles, postpartum challenges, career setbacks and shifting identities. Episodes alternate between workplace and domestic settings as the ensemble makes difficult choices, leans on — and tests — one another, and copes with the messy, often comedic fallout of trying to “have it all.” The tone moves fluidly between sharp humor and candid drama as the characters wrestle with ambition, guilt, intimacy and the practical logistics of raising children in an urban environment.
properties.genre_description: A single-camera comedy-drama (dramedy) that mixes sitcom-style situational humor with serialized dramatic storytelling. Episodes are structured around short, comedic set-pieces and character-driven arcs that accumulate across a season, combining the pacing and punchlines of contemporary workplace/family comedies with deeper, ongoing interpersonal conflict typical of hour-long dramas.
properties.style_description: Visually realistic and contemporary, favoring naturalistic lighting, intimate domestic and office locations, and unobtrusive camerawork that highlights performances. Direction emphasizes quick-witted dialogue, timing-driven comedic beats, and close-ups for emotional payoff. The series balances polished production values with a candid, observational aesthetic that underscores its blend of humor and drama.

properties.plot_themes_description: The series explores motherhood and the many forms it takes, the limits and supports of friendship, questions of personal and professional identity, and the pressure to balance work and family. Secondary themes include mental health (postpartum depression and anxiety), gender expectations, modern relationship dynamics, career ambition versus caregiving, and the negotiation of autonomy and interdependence within families.
properties.emotional_tone_description: Warmly irreverent and often brutally honest, the show blends sharp, witty comedy with moments of emotional vulnerability. Viewers can expect to laugh at awkward, relatable situations and to be moved by frank depictions of burnout, grief, and reconciliation. Overall the affect oscillates between cathartic levity and trenchant poignancy.

properties.description: Young Sheldon (2017) is a period prequel sitcom created by Chuck Lorre and Steven Molaro that chronicles the childhood of a brilliant but socially awkward nine-year-old in East Texas. The series stars Iain Armitage as the child prodigy, with Zoe Perry and Lance Barber among the principal cast, and features narration by the adult version of the character. Tonally it mixes sitcom humor with emotional, character-driven family drama and recurring themes of belonging, faith, and neurodiversity. The show leans on nostalgic production design and affectionate performances to balance comedy with poignant coming-of-age moments.
properties.plot_summary: Set in East Texas in the late 1980s and early 1990s, the story follows a nine-year-old child prodigy who skips grades to attend high school and struggles to fit in. His extraordinary intellect frequently clashes with emotional immaturity and social cluelessness, producing comic misunderstandings and heartfelt tensions. The series also centers on his working-class family and their efforts to support one another amid economic and personal pressures. Adult narration frames the episodes, adding reflective, often humorous perspective on the events of his childhood.

properties.description: The Baker and the Beauty (2020) is a U.S. romantic comedy-drama adaptation of an Israeli series that follows a blue-collar baker who begins a romance with an international superstar. Starring Victor Rasuk, Nathalie Kelley, and Dan Bucatinsky, the show blends comedy and heartfelt family drama to examine fame, class differences, and cultural identity. Across its episodes the series balances light humor and sincere emotional moments, emphasizing family bonds and the challenges that sudden visibility brings.
properties.plot_summary: A working-class baker in Miami strikes up an unlikely romance with an international superstar, forcing both to navigate the pressures of fame, family expectations, and cultural differences. As their relationship deepens, intimate family dynamics and personal identities come into sharper focus, revealing the comical and tender consequences of two very different worlds colliding. The series balances lighthearted humor with emotional stakes, following both partners and their families as they adjust to shifting roles and new possibilities.

properties.description: Not Dead Yet (2023) is a comedy-drama television series that follows Nell Serrano, a formerly successful journalist starting over after a major setback who takes a job writing obituaries and discovers she can see and converse with the recently deceased. Starring Gina Rodriguez, the series blends workplace comedy with gentle supernatural elements and character-led drama. Directed across episodes by a team of episodic television directors, the show combines situational humor in a newsroom setting with emotionally resonant, serialized arcs. Themes include life and death, redemption, second chances, and the rebuilding of personal and professional identity; its emotional tone is warm, witty, and quietly restorative.
properties.plot_summary: A once-prominent journalist hit by a major personal and professional setback reluctantly rebuilds her life by taking a job writing obituaries. As she researches the final chapters of other people’s lives she begins to see and converse with the recently deceased, whose blunt, funny, and sometimes painful interventions force her to confront her own regrets and ambitions. Each episode pairs workplace rhythms and reporting deadlines with quiet, supernatural encounters that reveal secrets, repair relationships, and deliver unexpected wisdom. Through these encounters she re-learns how to trust, to take creative risks, and to connect with both the living colleagues around her and the lingering spirits who push her toward second chances.

properties.description: Private Eyes is a Canadian comedy-drama (premiering in 2016) that pairs a former professional hockey player with a pragmatic private investigator as they run a detective agency in Toronto. Starring Jason Priestley, Cindy Sampson and Barry Flatman, the show mixes episodic crime-solving with serialized character beats, balancing mystery and procedural elements with humor and family dynamics. Recurring themes include partnership, trust, and community, and the series' tone is warm, witty, and character-driven. The visual approach emphasizes naturalistic, polished photography that showcases the city and the chemistry between the leads.
properties.plot_summary: A former professional hockey player teams up with a no-nonsense private investigator to run a detective agency that takes on cases across Toronto. The partnership blends procedural mystery with lighthearted, witty banter as the two navigate suspects, clues, and the city's neighborhoods. Episodes balance stand-alone investigations with character moments that reveal family ties, personal vulnerabilities, and evolving trust. The tone is warm and often comedic while retaining suspense around each case.
